jobs.occupation: Staff Scientist as Parental Leave Replacement (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description:
The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.

We investigate how cancer develops, identify cancer risk factors and search for new cancer prevention strategies. We develop new methods with which tumors can be diagnosed more precisely and cancer patients can be treated more successfully. Every contribution counts – whether in research, administration or infrastructure. This is what makes our daily work so meaningful and exciting.

The Single-cell Open Lab at the German Cancer Research Center is seeking, starting in January 2027, a Staff Scientist as Parental Leave Replacement.

The Single-cell Open Lab (scOpenLab) provides state-of-the-art infrastructure and scientific expertise for single-cell sequencing and spatial omics. Our goal is to enable researchers to perform advanced experiments independently: we advise users on experimental design, provide hands-on training, and support them throughout project optimization, experimental implementation, and library preparation.

Our technology portfolio covers a broad range of single-cell and multi-omic approaches, including single-cell RNA, DNA, and chromatin profiling, as well as spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics. Beyond providing access to established technologies, method development is an important part of our work. We continuously evaluate, adapt, and establish emerging single-cell and spatial technologies and develop customized experimental workflows. Examples include HIPSDR-seq for joint single-cell DNA and RNA profiling and the implementation of new spatial omics approaches. The scOpenLab is also closely involved in MultiSpace, the platform for spatial omics within the Health + Life Science Alliance Heidelberg Mannheim. Through MultiSpace, we collaborate with other technology platforms and research groups to enable multimodal spatial profiling and the integration of spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, and other molecular readouts.

Your Tasks

We are looking for a research scientist to cover a period of parental leave and join our interdisciplinary team. The position combines user support and training with hands-on experimental work and technology development, offering the opportunity to work at the forefront of rapidly evolving single-cell and spatial omics technologies with the following tasks:

- Planning and designing spatially resolved transcriptome and proteomics projects with our users
- Training of new users for spatial and single-cell omics assays
- Optimization and integration of new methods in the lab with a focus on multimodal approaches
- Organizing and driving early access programmes
- Scheduling and maintenance of service infrastructure for image-based spatial transcriptomics

Your Profile

- University degree in life science (MSc), additional PhD preferred
- Experience and very good knowledge of NGS techniques, library preparation, tissue handling, and imaging (skills in data analysis are a plus)
- Previous work in the single-cell field is certainly an advantage
- Very good knowledge of English and German
- Self-motivation and innovative thinking will be required for the successful implementation of your work. This also includes excellent communication and organizational skills.

Please provide both a CV and a cover letter.

We Offer

- Excellent framework conditions: state-of-the-art equipment and opportunities for international networking at the highest level
- 30 days of vacation per year
- Flexible working hours
- Remuneration according to TV-L incl. occupational pension plan and capital-forming payments
- Possibility of part-time work
- Family-friendly working environment
- Sustainable travel to work: subsidized Germany job ticket
- Unleash your full potential: targeted offers for your personal development to further develop your talents
- Our Corporate Health Management Program offers a holistic approach to your well-being

Are you interested?

Then become part of the DKFZ and join us in contributing to a life without cancer!

Contact:

Dr. Jan-Philipp Mallm
Phone: +49 (0)6221/54-51378

​Duration: The position is initially limited until 31.12.2027. An extension is possible.

Application Deadline: October 22, 2026

jobs.occupation: Administrative Lab Technician (Biologielaborant/in)
jobs.description:
The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.

We investigate how cancer develops, identify cancer risk factors and search for new cancer prevention strategies. We develop new methods with which tumors can be diagnosed more precisely and cancer patients can be treated more successfully. Every contribution counts – whether in research, administration or infrastructure. This is what makes our daily work so meaningful and exciting.

Our Junior Research Group "Epithelium Microbiome Interactions" (headed by Dr. Jens Puschhof) is seeking, starting at the earliest date possible, a Administrative Lab Technician.

In the EMIL group, we study how bacteria contribute to cancer development, metastasis, and treatment response. Our team includes cancer researchers, tissue engineers, microbiologists, and bioinformaticians working together to help patients by deciphering the functional impacts of bacteria in human tumors.
Using tissue samples from patients, we isolate bacterial strains and create organoids. These models can be combined with additional features of the human gut on USB stick-sized devices, “organ chips”, for detailed studies. We transplant organoid-bacteria mixtures into mouse models to study their migration and interaction in a whole-body context.
In our unique biobank at DKFZ, we characterize both tumor organoids and tumor-resident bacterial strains through whole genome sequencing, fluorescence microscopy, and other cutting-edge methods. Based on the diverse data obtained, we develop hypotheses about how specific bacterial species might influence tumors. With our broad portfolio of patient-derived models, our main focus lies on testing these relationships. Through close collaborations with clinical partners, we work towards the rapid translation of our findings into new microbiome-based strategies for the detection, prevention, and treatment of cancer.

Your Tasks

- Organization and coordination of day-to-day laboratory operations, including inventory management, procurement, equipment maintenance, shipping, and logistics
- Coordination of occupational safety, biosafety, and laboratory safety procedures, including support with regulatory documentation and internal inspections
- Organization and quality control of shared consumables, reagents, and laboratory spaces
- Experimental and administrative management of the organoid biobank and bacterial strain collection
- Performance and coordination of key laboratory assays, particularly genotyping and mycoplasma testing
- Onboarding, practical instruction, and supervision of students and new group members
- Communication and coordination with suppliers, service providers, internal DKFZ units, and external collaboration partners

Your Profile

- Completed vocational training as a laboratory technician or an equivalent qualification
- Very good practical knowledge of biological and/or molecular biology laboratory work and laboratory organization
- Ideally, experience with inventory management, procurement, equipment coordination, and laboratory documentation
- Knowledge of occupational safety, biosafety, and relevant documentation requirements is an advantage
- Independent, structured, and reliable working style with strong organizational skills
- Very good communication and coordination skills when working with scientists, students, internal service units, and external partners
- Motivation to work in a diverse role combining hands-on laboratory work with administrative and organizational responsibilities
- Very good written and spoken English and German

- Excellent framework conditions: state-of-the-art equipment and opportunities for international networking at the highest level
- 30 days of vacation per year

jobs.occupation: PhD Measuring and Scaling Agentic Software Engineering (f/m/x) (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
Stellenreferenz: 195022

Our brands BMW, MINI, Rolls-Royce and BMW Motorrad have made us one of the world's leading premium manufacturer of cars and motorcycles as well as provider of premium financial and mobility services.

THE FUTURE IS WHAT WE CREATE WHEN WE TAKE OUR VISIONS TO THE LIMITS.

PHD AT THE BMW GROUP.

Bridging the gap between your doctoral studies and the kind of career challenge you’re looking for isn’t always easy. That’s why our ProMotion PhD programme gives you the opportunity to apply your passion and scientific expertise to very real challenges that could shape the future of mobility. If selected, you’ll have the chance to really develop your own future career path with us through your practice-related thesis, promote your chosen specialty from within – and position yourself to secure the career you’ve always wanted.

Our New Technologies team explores and evaluates emerging technologies and brings the most promising ones into productive use across the BMW Group. Agentic software engineering is one of these technologies, and as a PhD candidate, you help find ways to systematically measure agentic software development and scale it to real-world use.

What awaits you?

- You design benchmarks that evaluate coding agents on real automotive codebases across the full development lifecycle.
- Within this project, you investigate where agents lose relevant code between exploration and generation - a failure mode that grows with codebase size and remains unmeasured.
- Building on these insights, you explore methods that help agents preserve and use relevant code more effectively.
- In this role, you help develop verification and testing approaches that keep agent-generated code trustworthy without slowing down development.
- Together with the team, you benchmark agent configurations, LLMs, harnesses and scaffolding across heterogeneous stacks such as embedded C/C++, Java, Python and Go.
- Finally, you translate your findings into research and deployment frameworks that can be applied at real-world scale.

What should you bring along?

- Studies in computer science, data science, mathematics or a comparable field.
- Solid knowledge of machine learning, in particular large language models and agentic systems.
- Strong programming skills in Python; experience with C/C++, Java or Go is an advantage.
- Hands-on experience with agent evaluation and benchmarking, for example SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, tau-bench or comparable frameworks.
- Ideally first publications or submissions at relevant scientific venues during your studies.
- Very good English language skills; German is an advantage.

Are you excited about advancing the science and practice of agentic software engineering at automotive scale? Apply now!

Note: Please apply exclusively online through our career portal. Applications submitted via other channels (including email) cannot be considered. Citizens of countries outside the European Union must have a valid residence or work permit for the duration of the program.

If you make it to the next round, you will receive an invitation to a video interview by e-mail. Please also check your spam folder regularly.

What do we offer?

- Comprehensive mentoring & onboarding.
- Personal & professional development.
- Flexible working hours.
- Digital offers & mobile working.
- Attractive & fair remuneration.
- Annual special payments such as vacation pay and Christmas bonus.
- Apartment offers for students (subject to availability & only Munich).
- And many other benefits –see bmw.jobs/benefits

Start date: 02.11.2026

Duration: 36 months

The mission of Testability is to maximize the visibility and transparency of a system's internal state through intentional design.
